summary: AI observability has become essential as LLM deployments scale, with the market growing to an estimated $2.69 billion in 2026 and projected to reach $9.26 billion by 2030 at a 36.2% CAGR. Without proper monitoring, teams operate blind to hallucinations, latency spikes, prompt regressions, and runaway API costs that can silently erode both quality and budget. Gartner predicts LLM observability investments will account for 50% of GenAI deployments by 2028, up from just 15% in early 2026, underscoring how rapidly it has shifted from optional to critical infrastructure.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: LLM traces, chain execution steps, agent runs, prompt versions, and evaluation datasets across LangChain and non-LangChain pipelines
features: End-to-end trace visualization for chains and agents
Prompt versioning and management
Dataset creation and regression testing
Human and automated evaluation workflows
Latency and token usage breakdowns per run
Integration with LangChain ecosystem out of the box
tools.pricing: Developer tier free at 5,000 traces/month; Plus at $39/seat/month with overage around $2.50 per 1,000 traces at standard retention; Enterprise pricing available
tools.best_for: Teams building with LangChain who need tight prompt management, evaluation datasets, and regression testing in a single platform

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API requests, costs, latency, token usage, error rates, and prompt performance across providers via a proxy gateway
features: One-line proxy integration requiring minimal setup (approx. 2 minutes)
Real-time cost tracking and budget alerts per user or session
Request caching to reduce redundant API calls
Rate limiting and access control
Prompt templating and version comparison
Open-source and self-hostable with managed cloud option
SOC-2 Type II and HIPAA compliance on Team tier
tools.pricing: Free Hobby tier at 10,000 requests/month; Pro at $79/month (unlimited seats, usage-based beyond included volume); Team at $799/month (compliance features); Enterprise custom pricing with SAML SSO and on-prem options. Managed cloud approximately £20/month for 100K requests.
tools.best_for: Teams that prioritize cost visibility and fast setup, especially those needing a lightweight API gateway with built-in monitoring rather than deep evaluation workflows

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B Weave)
tools.monitors: LLM traces, experiments, model evaluation metrics, dataset versions, and end-to-end ML pipeline artifacts
features: Experiment tracking tightly integrated with model training workflows
Weave module for LLM-specific tracing and evaluation
Dataset and artifact versioning across the full ML lifecycle
Collaborative dashboards for comparing model runs
Online and offline evaluation support
Strong integration with PyTorch, HuggingFace, and major LLM frameworks
tools.pricing: Free tier available for individuals; Teams plan at $50/seat/month; Enterprise pricing on request. Storage and compute costs apply for large artifact volumes.
tools.best_for: ML-native teams who are already using W&B for model training and want to extend observability seamlessly into LLM fine-tuning and production evaluation without adopting a separate tool

tools.name: Arize AI (Arize Phoenix)
tools.monitors: LLM spans and traces, embedding drift, retrieval quality in RAG pipelines, latency, error rates, and enterprise-scale telemetry
features: Span-level tracing with detailed latency and error dashboards
Experiment-style workflows for comparing model or prompt runs
Embedding drift detection for production monitoring
RAG retrieval quality evaluation and chunk-level inspection
OpenTelemetry-native instrumentation
Phoenix open-source version available for local and self-hosted use
Enterprise telemetry and compliance features in Arize cloud
tools.pricing: Arize Phoenix is open-source and free to self-host; Arize cloud platform has a free Developer tier, with Growth and Enterprise plans priced on volume and features — contact sales for enterprise quotes
tools.best_for: Enterprise teams needing production-grade telemetry, embedding drift detection, and RAG evaluation at scale, with the option to start locally via the open-source Phoenix package

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, prompt versions, token usage, latency, custom evaluation scores, and user session flows
features: Detailed LLM tracing with nested span support
Prompt management with versioning and A/B testing hooks
Custom scoring API for human and automated evaluations
Native DeepEval and other evaluation framework integrations
Self-hosting option for full data control under MIT license
Strong community adoption and active open-source development
SDKs for Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, and OpenAI-compatible wrappers
tools.pricing: Langfuse Cloud free for under 50,000 requests/month; paid cloud tiers start around £20/month for higher volumes (up to 500K events); Self-hosted is free with infrastructure costs estimated around £30/month plus approximately 2 hours of maintenance per month
tools.best_for: Open-source-first teams who need flexible tracing, prompt management, and custom evaluation scoring with the option to self-host for full data sovereignty

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM calls, token usage, latency, and errors across providers using OpenTelemetry-standard instrumentation
features: OpenTelemetry-native SDK for automatic LLM call instrumentation
Works with any OTel-compatible backend such as Grafana, Jaeger, or Honeycomb
Supports major LLM providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, and more
Vendor-neutral approach avoids lock-in to a proprietary observability platform
Lightweight integration requiring minimal code changes
Open-source under Apache 2.0 license
tools.pricing: Fully open-source and free; backend storage and visualization costs depend on the OTel-compatible platform chosen by the team
tools.best_for: Engineering teams already invested in OpenTelemetry infrastructure who want to add LLM observability without adopting a new proprietary tool, routing data to their existing observability stack

tools.name: Confident AI (DeepEval)
tools.monitors: LLM output quality, hallucination, relevance, toxicity, bias, RAG faithfulness, and 50+ evaluation metrics across development and production
features: 50+ open-source evaluation metrics via the DeepEval library
Integrated observability layer that runs DeepEval metrics on live production traffic
Regression testing CI/CD integration for prompt and model changes
RAG pipeline evaluation including context precision and recall
Used by OpenAI, Google, and Microsoft teams according to vendor claims
Dashboard for tracking metric trends over time in production
tools.pricing: DeepEval OSS library is free and open-source; Confident AI cloud platform offers a free tier with paid plans for higher evaluation volumes and team collaboration — contact vendor for current pricing
tools.best_for: Teams that prioritize evaluation depth and want to run rigorous automated quality checks across both CI/CD pipelines and live production traffic using a unified metrics framework

tools.name: OpenObserve
tools.monitors: LLM traces, prompts, and costs alongside full infrastructure observability including logs, metrics, application traces, and frontend Real User Monitoring (RUM) in a single platform
features: Unified LLM and infrastructure observability eliminating the need for a separate DevOps telemetry stack
Prompt tracing and cost tracking for LLM workloads
Log aggregation, metrics collection, and distributed tracing
Frontend RUM monitoring integrated in the same deployment
Open-source and self-hostable with a managed cloud option
Significantly lower storage costs compared to Elasticsearch-based alternatives
tools.pricing: Open-source self-hosted version is free; OpenObserve Cloud offers a free tier with consumption-based paid tiers — check the vendor site for current volume pricing
tools.best_for: Platform or DevOps teams who want to consolidate LLM observability with their existing infrastructure monitoring rather than running and maintaining two separate toolchains

cost_tips: Implement prompt caching and request deduplication: tools like Helicone offer built-in caching so semantically identical or repeated requests return cached responses without hitting the LLM API, which can reduce costs by 20–40% for applications with repetitive query patterns such as FAQs or templated workflows

Right-size your model selection per task: use cheaper, smaller models such as GPT-4o-mini or Claude Haiku for classification, summarization, or routing tasks, and reserve larger frontier models only for complex reasoning steps — tracing tools like Langfuse or LangSmith make it straightforward to profile which calls actually require high-capability models versus which are over-provisioned

Set token budgets and monitor usage at the session and user level: establish per-user or per-session token limits using observability dashboards, and alert on anomalous consumption before it compounds — cost monitoring tools like Helicone and Arize provide granular breakdowns that help identify runaway agent loops or unexpectedly verbose prompts that inflate token counts

Continuously evaluate and trim prompt length through prompt management workflows: bloated system prompts, redundant context, and over-stuffed few-shot examples are a leading cause of unnecessary token spend — using prompt versioning in tools like Langfuse or LangSmith allows teams to A/B test shorter prompt variants against quality metrics, finding the minimum effective prompt that meets output quality thresholds without paying for excess tokens
